findings.summary: Bazel is a free, open-source build and test automation tool originally derived from Google's internal Blaze system. It uses the Starlark language to define build rules and macros, enabling reproducible builds across multiple programming languages within a single repository. Bazel employs sandboxing during compilation to enforce dependency isolation, requiring explicit input/output specification to support hermetic builds and cross-user caching. It supports a wide range of languages and can produce deployable artifacts for Android and iOS platforms.

mechanisms.title: Starlark-based build rules
mechanisms.explanation: Build targets, rules, and macros are authored in Starlark, a Python-dialect language restricted from file I/O to prevent side-effects and ensure dependency-graph integrity.

mechanisms.title: Sandboxed compilation
mechanisms.explanation: Bazel creates a sandbox directory filled with symlinks to explicit input dependencies during compilation, preventing unintended header inclusion and enforcing declared dependency boundaries.
